gitCommit.subject: Make playbook curation a recurring daily exercise, not a one-off cleanup (#250)
gitCommit.body:
Make playbook curation a recurring daily exercise, not a one-off cleanup (#250)

Mukesh chose option (b) - archive superseded per-run notes into an
appendix the curator is not given - then: "make this exercise of curating
the playbook as a regular exercise instead of a one time task."

docs/attacker-playbook.md is loaded WHOLE into two prompts, the curator
twice daily and pr-security-review.mjs on every PR, and every pass appends
a note. On 2026-08-26 it silently overflowed the curator's body budget and
produced five consecutive mornings of a wrong A5 count; the budget had
been raised twice for the same reason, including this morning at 99% full.

Two things make it recurring. It runs from the morning routine as a
--check dry-run in the SessionStart hook beside context hygiene, printing
live size as a percentage of the curator budget. And it archives on AGE
rather than everything it can: notes age out of a 14-day retention window,
so recent history stays visible while old repetition leaves. That turns
unbounded growth into a steady state, which was always the goal - the
one-time cut never was.

The window was chosen by measurement and my first answer was wrong. 30
days parks the file at 69%, ON the 70% alarm, where the alarm's own advice
is useless because everything is still inside the window. Measured: 30d
219 KB (69%), 21d 203 KB (63%), 14d 194 KB (61%), 10d 183 KB (57%), 7d
149 KB (47%). The alarm now names both levers in order and still says do
not raise the budget.

Three defects in my own work, each caught by checking: the KEEP guard
protected 0 blocks and was indistinguishable from one that cannot fire;
the block parser orphaned nested bullets so an archived note's children
stayed behind still asserting a superseded count; and I shipped the policy
before the state, archiving everything while the policy said keep 14 days.

The retention window then broke the count parser, which is the sharpest
find. extractAtoPassCount takes the last "running count -> N" in document
order - safe while notes were appended chronologically, unsafe the moment
a current-status digest sat above retained notes quoting older counts. On
the full file it was right only by luck; truncated to 25k it returned 18
against a live 24. The digest bullet is now marked AUTHORITATIVE and the
parser prefers it, falling back to the positional read.

Document order is a proxy for recency, and it silently stops being one the
moment you put a summary above the history it summarises.

First pass under the real policy: 249,085 -> 193,921 chars (-55,164, 22%),
zero content loss verified line by line, inventory unchanged at 12 ## /
62 ###, count reads 24 through the real parser.

+16 tests, all mutation-checked. npm run verify green: 477 files / 5338
tests. iOS accounting: ZERO, checked by consumer.
